causes.text: In late June 2025, SLB (Schlumberger) told investors it expected second-quarter revenue and core profit to be roughly flat due to weaker drilling activity in Saudi Arabia and Latin America and an unfavorable geographic mix weighing on margins.

source_info.title: SLB expects flat quarterly revenue, profit amid weaker activity in Saudi Arabia, Latin America

causes.text: By mid-June 2025, U.S. drillers had cut oil and gas rigs for the seventh straight week to the lowest level since 2021, signaling weaker near-term North American oilfield services demand.

source_info.title: US drillers cut oil/gas rigs for 7th week to lowest since 2021, Baker Hughes says

effects.text: On July 22, 2025, Halliburton reported second-quarter profit down about 33% to roughly $472 million, with revenue down 5.5% to $5.51 billion, citing weaker demand in North America and parts of the Middle East and a softer market outlook.

source_info.title: Halliburton forecasts steep full-year revenue decline on softer demand

causal_reasoning_chain.description: SLB warned of unexpectedly weaker activity in Saudi Arabia and Latin America and an unfavorable geographic mix, signaling sector-wide margin pressure.
U.S. rig counts kept falling through June 2025 to the lowest since 2021, pointing to softer North American services demand.
These external signals transmitted through pricing and utilization to Halliburton, with both international (Saudi/Kuwait) and North American exposure facing headwinds.
On July 22, 2025, Halliburton reported a ~33% Q2 profit drop and a weaker outlook; shares traded down roughly 0.7% on the day.

rationale: A combination of regional slowdowns flagged by a major competitor (SLB) and a sustained decline in U.S. rig activity created dual external headwinds for oilfield services providers. These pressures reduced Halliburton's utilization and pricing, contributing to lower revenue and profit and a modest share-price decline on results day.
counterfactual_analysis: If SLB had not flagged slowdowns in Saudi Arabia/Latin America and U.S. rig counts had stabilized or risen, Halliburton would likely have seen firmer activity and utilization, reducing the profit decline and limiting the negative stock reaction.

adversarial_confounders.text: Company-specific execution issues or cost overruns unrelated to sector-wide demand could depress results.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Would weaken the explanatory power of external slowdowns for Halliburton's quarterly performance.

adversarial_confounders.text: Macro variables-FX, tariffs, and commodity-price volatility-may simultaneously affect rig counts and Halliburton's earnings.
adversarial_confounders.impact: Could act as common causes that inflate the apparent effect of competitor warnings and rig-count declines.

details.commentary: Weaker drilling in Saudi Arabia, Latin America and the U.S. shifted bargaining power toward oil and gas producers that were curbing activity. In that environment, integrated service providers like Halliburton had to accept lower utilization and margin pressure rather than risk losing scarce work to rivals.

details.pestel_factor: Economic - activity slowdown in Saudi/Latin America and falling U.S. rig counts
details.commentary: Softening commodity demand and regional spending pullbacks created a less supportive macro backdrop for oilfield services. Those economic signals foreshadowed the weaker second-quarter results and more cautious outlook that Halliburton later reported.

Rig declines and slower customer activity fed through to lower volumes and a less favorable geographic mix, cutting Halliburton's profit by a third. The disappointing quarter and softer guidance then reinforced E&P budget discipline, making it harder for North American and Middle Eastern activity to rebound quickly.
